ANAGRAMMATIC - C48 PILOT CHECKPOINT

New C48 source: src/anagram.c
ZX-UX executable: bin/ssx/anagram.ssx
Native ZX-UX cassette: bin/tzx/anagram.tzx, on-tape name anagram

Controls: any key opens input; enter rearranged letters, then Enter;
Y or N states whether fixed letters exist. With Y, supply known pattern
using - for open positions; with N, enter starting word length and Enter.
Combinations are generated from the supplied letters using separate
positions for repeats. Q exits at the end of an output run.

RVM input replay: --keys '{WAIT 80}{SPACE}AE\nN2\n'
Expected result: AE and EA, followed by completion text.
Reproduce the native emulator frames with:
    python3 -B tools/bonus_fuse.py --case anagram:intro [...]
    python3 -B tools/bonus_fuse.py --case anagram:main [...]
    python3 -B tools/bonus_fuse.py --case anagram:result [...]
The command's --help lists the required host paths and switches.

Visual review: BASIC screenshots 01-INTRO, 02-MAIN and 03-AFTER-INPUT
were inspected beside genuine C48 RVM and native FUSE captures. Intro
color, input flow, and visible arrangement output agree in purpose.
The required ZX-UX font64 gives different text density and spacing.
Live output may contain additional arrangements when sampled later.

Known limit: up to 8 freely entered letters; the BASIC listing has no
such fixed eight-letter input cap. This is a port limitation, not a
complete claim of equal behavior for arbitrary inputs. Input replay in
FUSE may sample different output stages than the deterministic RVM test.

Native FUSE and RVM runs were performed using the real ZX-UX kernel.
See tests/test_bonus_pilots.py for executable replay checks.
